walkthroughs.body_html:
UK in the 21st Century — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

UK in the 21st Century brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with UK in the 21st Century.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The San Andreas Fault is what type of margin?
options: Constructive
Destructive
Conservative
Collision

mcqs.q: What happens at a constructive (divergent) plate boundary?
options: Plates move apart, magma rises to fill the gap and solidifies, forming new oceanic crust — for example at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.
At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
At constructive boundaries the plates collide and build mountains.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between biotic and abiotic components of an ecosystem?
options: Biotic and abiotic both refer to types of soil.
Biotic means animals and abiotic means plants.
Biotic components are all living organisms (plants, animals, microbes); abiotic components are non-living factors (climate, soil, water, light, rock).
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the focus and epicentre of an earthquake?
options: The focus (hypocentre) is the underground point where the earthquake originates; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
The focus and epicentre are the same point.
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.
